audit.why: 52.72% Emerald+ over 43 real games, EVEN at 5.5/10. Sion has exactly one kill pattern before 6 — a fully-charged Decimating Smash into a Soul Furnace detonation — and no way to catch a Riftwalking Kassadin afterwards. The chart already gives him only Level 1 and that is right.

Level 1 Sion, Level 2 Skill, Level 3 onward Kassadin, on both win[] and phases[].side, and every caption agrees with its side. This is the only matchup in my slice whose chart needed nothing. The spikes match too: the kill window is 1-3, Riftwalk at 6, Rod of Ages at first item, blink-kiting at 2+.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four things. (a) The packet is right that the content layer never names a single Sion ability — it says 'his Q', 'the W detonation', 'his E shred-line' throughout, so a reader cannot map the advice onto what they see on screen. (b) content late says 'his Void Stone is irrelevant since you simply outrun a tank'. Void Stone is Kassadin's own passive; Sion does not have it. (c) early and wants.foe[1] call Roar of the Slayer an 'armor/MR shred line'. Riot's text is 'damages and slows and reduces the Armor of the first enemy hit' — Armor only, no Magic Resist. (d) breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0] and report[5] all say to 'break the channel' on Decimating Smash. Riot describes it as a charge, sion.json carries no channel flag on Q, and nothing in Kassadin's kit interrupts it — the real counterplay is that a Smash released before full charge deals damage but does not knock up or stun at all.
audit.why: Riot's Decimating Smash text: 'Sion charges a powerful swing in an area in front of himself that will deal damage to enemies when released. If he charges for enough time, enemies hit by the swing will also be knocked up and stunned.' The stun is conditional on charge time, which is the fact that makes sidestepping worth doing.
audit.corrected: Decimating Smash, Soul Furnace, Roar of the Slayer, Unstoppable Onslaught and Glory in Death are all named now. The Void Stone misattribution is gone. Roar of the Slayer is Armor shred only. 'Break the channel' is replaced with the full-charge condition and a perpendicular sidestep.

audit.whatIsWrong: Glory in Death is not mentioned anywhere on either layer.
audit.why: Riot: 'After being killed, Sion will temporarily reanimate with rapidly decaying Health. His attacks become very rapid, heal him, and deal bonus damage based on his target's maximum Health.' A squishy blink assassin who kills Sion and then stands next to the body is the exact target that passive was written for, and max-health damage ignores the fact that you built Rod of Ages.
audit.corrected: Named in whys[6], late, wants.foe[2], breakdown.cooldowns and loading, with the instruction to leave the corpse rather than keep attacking.

edits.before: Sion's whole early kill threat is the fully-charged Q knockup — if you stand in it at full charge it stuns you, his W detonation lands on a locked target, and pre-6 you have only Null Sphere's shield to answer with no blink to escape. Don't contest the wave: last-hit at max Q range and side-step the obvious charge by walking perpendicular to it. Use Nether Blade on a creep to refund your mana so you never get forced off lane, and just deny him the one full-charge Q he needs to commit. His E is an armor/MR-shred poke line, not a shield-break — it shreds your resists and shoves, it doesn't pop your Q shield.
edits.after: Sion's whole early kill threat is a fully-charged Decimating Smash (Q) — held long enough it knocks up and stuns, and Soul Furnace (W) detonates on a locked target while pre-6 you have only Null Sphere's shield and no blink. Don't contest the wave: last-hit at max Q range and walk perpendicular to the wind-up, because a Smash released early deals damage with no stun at all. Use Nether Blade on a creep to refund mana so you are never forced off lane. And read Roar of the Slayer (E) correctly — it shreds Armor and slows, not Magic Resist, and it does not touch your Q shield.

edits.before: Level 6 is where this lane stops being miserable. Riftwalk lets you blink straight over a charging Q or out of his E shred-line, so his only catch tool stops landing. Through 4-5 you farm defensively under tower with your maxed Q shield soaking his E poke, but once you hit Catalyst into Rod of Ages you climb past even and he can no longer freely shove you off the wave. Bait the Q charge with a feint, then blink in for a Force Pulse cone once it's burned — your E cooldown refunds fast off your own Riftwalk and Null Sphere casts.
edits.after: Level 6 is where this lane stops being miserable. Through 4-5 you farm defensively under tower with your maxed Q shield soaking his E poke, and once Catalyst becomes Rod of Ages you climb past even. Bait the Smash with a feint — 10s at rank 1, and released early it does not stun at all — then blink in for a Force Pulse cone once it's burned. Your E charges off your own Riftwalk and Null Sphere casts.

edits.before: This is the window the whole lane exists to reach. With Riftwalk stacking and Nashor's or Rabadon's online, you blink-kite Sion's completely immobile body forever — a slow-travel charged Q can never catch you, and his Void Stone is irrelevant since you simply outrun a tank. Ignore him in the splitpush and blink past his frontline in fights to delete the squishy he's protecting. Your only respect is a flank charged Q clipping your Riftwalk mid-engage — wait his Q out before you commit your blink into a teamfight.
